label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

report.summary: Outbox publications stalled after ~18:39:35 while transfers kept arriving. Delivery attempts to the consumer fail with connection errors, so notifications back up. Why the consumer refuses connections is not shown.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery stalled: 430 more events committed than published; publications fell from ~30/10s to 0 from about 18:39:35 on.
findings.reason: Per-bucket arrivals stayed at 30 while publications dropped to 0, and pending grew to 400.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts fail with CONNECTION_FAILED (3322 of 3613), taking about 0.25 ms each, while only 291 succeeded early in the window.
findings.reason: Failures return instantly with no status and no consumer record, consistent with refused connections to the consumer target.

findings.claim: The late notifications come from the consumer being unreachable, not from the database, pool or transfer API.
findings.reason: Transfers stay fast with no errors, the pool has no waits and there is no DB blocking, while the outbox backlog and failed count grow.

limitations: No consumer-side or network logs explain why connections were refused from about 18:39:35.
The oldest undelivered age of about 3400 s predates the window, so there was already a backlog; its origin is unseen.
next_checks: Check whether the consumer at 127.0.0.1:18090 was listening and healthy from about 18:39:35.
Review the 138 events already FAILED before the window and what retry or max-attempts handling applies.

alternatives.reason: No pool waits or timeouts and no blocking sessions were observed.
alternatives.hypothesis: DB pool exhaustion or lock contention slowing the outbox poller

alternatives.reason: Failures are instant connection failures, not 3 s timeouts; successful calls took about 71 ms.
alternatives.hypothesis: Slow consumer responses causing delivery timeouts
